question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Mughal emperor – city where he is buried / associated capital]
wrong_fact: Aurangzeb is buried at Khuldabad (near Aurangabad, Maharashtra), not in Delhi. He shifted his capital to Aurangabad in the Deccan during his campaigns and died there in 1707.
explanation: Akbar's tomb is at Sikandra, Agra. Jahangir is buried at Shahdara, Lahore (now in Pakistan). Shah Jahan was buried next to Mumtaz Mahal in the Taj Mahal in Agra. Aurangzeb, however, died in the Deccan and was buried at Khuldabad near Aurangabad (Maharashtra). The European trading factories flourished during the reign of these Mughals, especially under Akbar and Jahangir.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Mughal emperor – European trade concession / factory established during his reign]
options: Akbar – English East India Company received first audience at Agra (1583)
Jahangir – British ambassador Thomas Roe obtained farman for trade at Surat (1617)
Shah Jahan – British built their first factory at Hugli, Bengal during his reign
Aurangzeb – Portuguese established first European factory at Surat during his reign
wrong_fact: The Portuguese established their factory at Surat much earlier, during the reign of Jahangir (early 17th century), not Aurangzeb. The Portuguese arrived in India even before the Mughals consolidated power.
explanation: The English East India Company's first contact with Mughals was under Akbar. Thomas Roe's mission to Jahangir (1615–19) secured trading rights at Surat. The English established a factory at Hugli in Bengal around 1650 under Shah Jahan. Aurangzeb actually expelled the English from Bengal (Child's War, 1686–90) before granting limited trade rights again. The Portuguese were at Surat from the early 1600s under Jahangir.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Mughal governor (Subedar) / Nawab – his province / region in the context of European relations]
options: Murshid Quli Khan – Bengal (as Diwan and later Nawab)
Azim-us-Shan – Bihar (as Subedar when Siraj-ud-Daulah was young)
Mukarram Khan – Surat (as Mughal governor, dealing with European traders)
Daud Khan Panni – Arcot / Carnatic (as Mughal viceroy of the Deccan's eastern region)
wrong_fact: Azim-us-Shan was the Subedar of Bengal (not Bihar). He was the grandson of Aurangzeb who was posted in Bengal and was involved in early dealings with European powers there. Bihar was a separate sub-region under Bengal.
explanation: Murshid Quli Khan served as Diwan of Bengal under Aurangzeb and later became its first Nawab. Azim-us-Shan was the Mughal prince and Subedar of Bengal (not Bihar) under Aurangzeb. Mukarram Khan governed Surat and interacted with European traders. Daud Khan Panni served as Nawab of the Carnatic under the Mughals in the early 18th century, before the region came under independent Nawabs.
